title: Is Microsoft Getting Enough Credit for Better Free Cash Flow Compared to its Peers? | MSFT Stock
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; auto-captions garble names/numbers in places
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc compares Microsoft's quarter with its hyperscaler peers and praises its free cash flow discipline. Revenue was $92.3 billion, up 19% year over year, trailing Alphabet and Meta at 26% each, and operating income rose 21% with operating margins above 50%. Capital expenditure came in at $45.2 billion after third-party capacity deliveries were delayed, pushing revenue back since Microsoft has more demand than supply and hundreds of billions of dollars in backlog. The standout is cash: $58 billion of operating cash flow in the quarter, up 29%, which annualises to nearly $240 billion, and free cash flow of $18.6 billion. Microsoft is the only one of the four hyperscalers still free-cash-flow positive, while Alphabet, Meta and Amazon are heading into negative territory as they accelerate AI spending. He says he has criticised the haste of rivals' spending, but the verdict will take years, and contrasts Apple's approach of investing little in AI and licensing instead. No explicit buy, hold or sell verdict is given in the captions; his 25 October MSFT HOLD stands unchanged.
